title: Streptomycin, first antibiotic against tuberculosis
summary: As a graduate student in Selman Waksman's lab, Albert Schatz discovered the antibiotic streptomycin, reported in 1944.
why: The first effective drug treatment for tuberculosis.

unsung.contribution: Discovered the antibiotic streptomycin as a graduate student.
unsung.recognition: Waksman's accounts never mentioned him; a court affirmed him as co-discoverer, but the 1952 Nobel went to Waksman alone.
